content.value_statement: Paid ad teams need objective readbacks after budget, bid, or creative changes. This skill compares candidate and control windows, then records a clear Promote, Keep-testing, Rollback, or Unproven decision.
actual_capabilities: Defines a fixed readback window after the learning phase exits.
Compares ROAS or CPA against a control, not only before and after.
Normalizes attribution windows, currency, and conversion lag before comparison.
Labels figures as measured, user-provided, or estimated.
Prepares a handoff summary for paid measurement records.
limitations: Requires exported campaign, analytics, or ecommerce data from the user.
Does not compute ROAS or CPA ratios itself; it delegates that math.
Does not replace ad-platform API access or data exports.
Cannot prove causality when no valid control exists.

use_cases.description: Evaluate whether a paid campaign budget increase held ROAS versus an unchanged control.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Creative Rotation
use_cases.description: Decide whether a new creative should be promoted, tested longer, or rolled back.

use_cases.title: Compare Platform ROAS
use_cases.description: Normalize attribution windows and currency before comparing exported paid channel results.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Readback
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one campaign change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Read back my budget increase on Campaign X from July 1. I have spend, revenue, conversions, and a sibling control export.

prompt_templates.title: Creative Decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate the new prospecting creative launched on July 10. Compare it with the prior creative and tell me whether to promote, keep testing, or roll back.

prompt_templates.title: Cross-Platform Normalization
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Meta and Google ROAS from my exports. Normalize attribution windows and currency before you decide which result is stronger.

prompt_templates.title: Full Measurement Loop
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced readback with integrity checks and handoff.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a full paid measurement readback for my bid target change. Check learning phase, conversion lag, control validity, attribution integrity, and prepare the handoff summary.

output_examples.input: Budget increase for Campaign X with 14-day candidate and control exports.
output_examples.output: Decision: Keep-testing. Candidate ROAS improved 8 percent versus control, but the result did not pass the selected significance bar. Next readback date: July 22.

output_examples.input: New creative rotation with campaign export, ecommerce revenue export, and unchanged sibling ad set.
output_examples.output: Decision: Promote. The candidate beat the control on CPA and secondary conversion volume. Attribution window and currency were normalized before comparison.

output_examples.input: Meta and Google search exports with different attribution windows.
output_examples.output: Decision: Unproven. The exports used incompatible attribution windows, and no clean control was available. Normalize the windows before making a budget move.

best_practices: Set the readback window before looking at performance results.
Use an unchanged control measured over the same period.
Separate measured values from estimates and causal explanations.
anti_patterns: Do not call a raw before-and-after movement a win without a control.
Do not compare platform ROAS until attribution windows and currency match.
Do not promote results when tracking is broken or conversions are double-counted.

faq.question: What data does this skill need?
faq.answer: It needs the change date, campaign exports, conversion or revenue data, and a comparable control.

faq.question: Does it connect directly to ad platforms?
faq.answer: No. The skill is designed for user-provided exports. API connectors are optional conveniences.

faq.question: Can it calculate ROAS by itself?
faq.answer: No. It delegates ROAS and CPA arithmetic to a dedicated ROI calculator skill.

faq.question: What decisions can it return?
faq.answer: It returns Promote, Keep-testing, Rollback, or Unproven with the supporting measurement notes.

faq.question: How does it handle weak evidence?
faq.answer: It marks the result Unproven when the control is missing, attribution is dirty, or tracking is unreliable.

faq.question: Is it useful for cross-channel reporting?
faq.answer: It can support a paid readback, but broad cross-channel rollups belong in a performance analysis workflow.
